sentences.text: The genus Gallornis was first described by Lambrecht in 1931.
Because the fossil remains are too fragmentary to be confidently linked to Maniraptoromorpha, researchers have excluded it from many phylogenetic analyses.
Researchers propose that Gallornis fossils display features found only in Neornithes, the group of birds living today.
Evidence suggests that ancestors of all living birds formed a distinct evolutionary lineage from Hesperornithes and Ichthyornithes as early as 130 million years ago.
Gallornis lived alongside many non-avian dinosaurs around the Second Tethys Sea.
Gallornis was allied with the Paleocene Scaniornis to form the supposed family Scaniornithidae or Torotigidae, a hypothesis that may be incorrect.
A more probable hypothesis is that Gallornis was an early member of the Galloanserae clade, which includes modern landfowl and waterfowl.
The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Gallornis as Torotigidae.
The Paleobi Database lists the family of Gallornis as Torotigidae.
Gallornis straeleni lived approximately 140 to 130 million years ago near Auxerre in the Yonne department of France.
During its existence, the habitat was located around 30°N, north of the Tropic of Cancer aridity belt.
Given the hot and humid Cretaceous climate, the habitat likely resembled West Africa around the Gulf of Guinea.
The Paleobi Database records the time range of Gallornis as the Hauterivian stage, from 132.6 to 125.77 million years ago.
